items.title: Live Updates: Flight to Israel Is Diverted After Pilots Clash in Cockpit
items.summary: Passengers intervened after the pilot and co-pilot fought during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, forcing the plane to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. It was not clear what had prompted the clash.

items.title: Becerra and Hilton to Face Off in Televised California Governor Debate
items.summary: Xavier Becerra, a Democrat who served in the Biden administration, will debate Steve Hilton, a Republican former talk show host, in what’s likely to be their only face-off before the election.

items.title: Russia launches largest attack on Ukraine energy infrastructure since spring
items.summary: At least six people were killed and 33 others injured across the country in the overnight attacks, local authorities reported.

items.title: Last UK and US troops leave Iraq as anti-Islamic State mission ends
items.summary: The withdrawal of coalition forces, under a deal agreed two years ago, was a key demand of the Iraqi government.

items.title: After Two Decades, U.S. Forces Leave Iraq to an Uncertain Future
items.summary: Some Iraqis are celebrating the end of an American military presence that unleashed waves of bloodshed. Others fear what happens next for their country, trapped between Washington and Tehran.

items.title: American Forces Withdraw From Iraq 23 Years After Invading
items.summary: The Americans did not understand the country when they invaded in 2003. Over a correspondent’s many trips there, it was not clear that this ever changed much.

items.title: We need ‘right to intervene’ in AI amid growing threat, says Bank of England boss
items.summary: Andrew Bailey’s comments come as fears grow that rogue models could take financial system hostage Business live – latest updates The governor of the Bank of England has said authorities must retain the “right to intervene” in the AI industry amid growing fears that rogue models could take the financial system hostage. Andrew Bailey said the risks posed by the rapid advancement of frontier AI models – a number of which have gone rogue in recent months – were “real…

items.title: UK-France ‘one in one out’ deal to expire on Thursday, say sources
items.summary: Deal aimed at deterring small boat arrivals set to end as talks stall over French demand for EU-wide scheme UK politics live – latest updates The UK government’s “one in one out” deal with France, which was supposed to help deter small boat arrivals, is expected to expire on Thursday, government sources have said. items.summary: Northern Ireland secretary holding talks with both sides as Garvaghy Road group launches fresh legal challenge UK politics live – latest updates Talks to break the deadlock over the controversial Drumcree parade will continue with the Northern Ireland secretary, Chris Bryant, on Wednesday as nationalist protesters declare the prospect of mediation with unionists “dead in the water”. items.title: Judge Ends Federal Oversight of Oakland Police After 23 Years
items.summary: In ending the longest such monitoring in U.S. history, a federal court said the department had mostly complied with reforms mandated by a 2003 settlement after a police brutality lawsuit.

items.title: A Way Out of the A.I. Arms Race?
items.summary: New research points to how the world could stop short of the brink of disaster. Even with the agreement signed at the White House by tech leaders, it won’t be easy.

items.title: Greggs announces plans to shut four UK factories that could cost 740 jobs
items.summary: Bakery chain, whose sales are up 7.7%, says move is necessary to provide growth in ‘most cost-efficient manner’ Business live – latest updates Greggs has announced plans to close four of its factories, in a move that could result in 740 job losses over the next two and a half years. The bakery chain said it was consulting on the closures, which would initially cost £60m when including disruption costs and redundancy payments but then could create £20m of savings…

items.title: In Fractious France, Politicians Agree on One Thing: Pope Leo Was a Hit
items.summary: In a four-day visit, Pope Leo XIV won praise across the political spectrum, even from its most avowedly secular figures.

items.title: Ken Paxton, G.O.P. Nominee in Texas, Privately Said Trump’s Convention Hurt Him
items.summary: Ken Paxton, one of the party’s top Senate candidates and a Trump loyalist, said that “everybody’s numbers dropped” after the event, according to audio obtained by The Times.

items.title: Donor Gives $3 Billion to Carnegie Mellon, the Largest University Gift Ever
items.summary: Kenneth C. Griffin, the hedge fund executive, pledged to give $3 billion, much of it to build a campus in Miami.

items.title: 55 Swatting Calls: A Couple’s Fight Against Online Stalkers and the Police
items.summary: The city of Milwaukee agreed to a $575,000 settlement after months of heavily armed police responses to 911 calls to the couple’s home that officials knew were hoaxes.

items.title: As Violence Falls, Crime Isn’t Paying as a Republican Line of Attack
items.summary: Across the country, especially in the North Carolina Senate race, Republicans have charged opponents with being soft on crime, even as President Trump brags over plunging crime rates.

items.title: US actor Chad Lowe 'heartbroken' by death of daughter Fiona aged 13
items.summary: Lowe and his wife Kim Painter announce the death of their daughter, who "was the light of our lives".
